shared_elements: low relief carving in pale limestone
a row of repeated figures aligned along a horizontal register
horizontal band of repeating geometric pattern (net/chevron texture) separating or bordering zones
justification: Both surfaces organise profile figures into an evenly spaced horizontal row bounded by a band of repeating geometric texture, and both use shallow relief on pale stone, which is the most specific correspondence. But A is a single continuous, highly finished frieze of naturalistically modelled human figures with careful anatomical and textile detail, while B is a coarse, schematic multi-register pillar dominated by animals and stacked motifs, so the manner of carving and the overall composition read as entirely different.
